questions.question_english: 33. In football, which situation constitutes an 'Offside' offense?
options_english: A player deliberately handles the ball with their hand or arm inside their own team’s designated penalty box during active play.
A player in the opposition half is nearer to the opponent’s goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent when played.
An attacking player commits a reckless direct physical foul against the opposing goalkeeper within the six-yard goal area.
A field player executes an illegal restart by taking a throw-in using only one hand to propel the ball onto the pitch.
questions.explanation_english: An offside offense in football occurs when an attacking player is positioned in the opponent’s half and is nearer to the opponent’s goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent at the moment the ball is played by a teammate. This rule is governed by the Laws of the Game established by IFAB, which aims to prevent players from gaining an unfair advantage by being in a position that is too close to the opponent's goal.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: An offside offense in football occurs when an attacking player becomes involved in active play while positioned in the opponent’s half and nearer to the opponent’s goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.
